title: Same Fix, Different Weights: Replicating Weight-Space Programming with Claude

target_networks.name: Atari RAM PPO policies (Breakout, Pong, Ms. Pac-Man, Freeway)
Classic-control PPO policies (CartPole, Acrobot, MountainCar, LunarLander)
Character-level transformer middle blocks (Python, romaji, English)
9x9 Go policy network written by Claude

domain: reinforcement learning, games, interpretability, math reasoning

headline_result.text: Given Qwen3.5-0.8B's weights and 10, 25 or 50 practice forward passes, Claude Opus 5.5 raised MATH-500 from 6.7% to 51.4%, 55.2% and 58.1%, but by scaling the final norm (a temperature change that alone gives 20.9-22.1%) and the logits of 'Wait' and </think>, not by removing an internal loop direction.
headline_result.quote: Claude raised its MATH-500 score from 6.7% to 51.4%, 55.2% and 58.1% (500 problems × 4 samples; at 50 passes +51.4 points, 95% interval [47.9, 55.0], against the original’s 48.1%)

evidence_quality.n_runs_or_seeds: 3-5 attempts per network in most reading/fixing probes; single run per budget in Experiments 5b, 6 and 8

key_claims.claim: Every Qwen edit acted at the output side (final norm scaling plus 'Wait' and </think> logits) rather than removing an internal loop direction as the original did.
key_claims.quote: Unlike the original, which removed an internal loop direction, every edit acted at the output: it scaled the final norm, which raises the effective sampling temperature, and the logits of “Wait” and </think>.

key_claims.claim: A norm-only temperature control reproduces about a third of the MATH-500 gain and nearly all of the IFEval gain.
key_claims.quote: Temperature alone lifts MATH-500 to 22.1% (s = 0.6) and 20.9% (s = 0.68), about a third of the gain (28–35%), and GSM8K by about half (49–59%).

key_claims.claim: On Gemma 3 270M, which rarely loops, no edit helped, matching the original's null control.
key_claims.quote: On MATH-500 (n = 500 × 4) it moved the score from 9.2% to 8.3%, a change of −0.8 points [−1.9, +0.2], and the share at the 8,192-token limit from 4.6% to 2.0%.

key_claims.claim: Repairs and zero-shot policies were known textbook controllers grafted into a few units, not repairs of the learned circuit.
key_claims.quote: None of the ten repairs in Experiment 4 repaired the learned circuit. Each grafted a textbook controller into repurposed units; nine of the ten switched the trained units off

key_claims.claim: When asked what data a network was trained on, Claude fell back on priors (interface shape, dataset defaults, famous games).
key_claims.quote: When the question is about the training distribution, Claude falls back on priors. Three priors recur.

key_claims.claim: Claude identified all 10 untrained networks and found copying heads from weight products in 15 of 15 runs.
key_claims.quote: All 10 untrained networks were called untrained.

limitations_stated.text: One Claude run per budget in Experiment 8, so the budget comparison covers evaluation noise, not run-to-run spread.
limitations_stated.quote: Each budget has one Claude run, as in the original, so the budget comparison (+6.8 points [4.9, 8.7] from 10 to 50 passes on MATH-500) is a comparison of three runs.

limitations_stated.text: The practice tool returned per-layer mean activations that the original does not describe, which may have made the task easier.
limitations_stated.quote: This is more information than generations alone, and it may have made the task easier than the original’s.

limitations_stated.text: Pre-registration fixed grading, not design, and was not deposited with a third party.
limitations_stated.quote: Pre-registration fixed grading, not design, and it was not deposited with a third party or timestamped externally.

notes_for_review: The most complete independent replication: all eight MIT probes with Claude Opus 5.5, internal pre-registered grading rules, untrained and permutation controls, and a norm-only temperature control for the Qwen edit. The Qwen MATH-500 gain replicates in size but by a different mechanism, and about a third of it equals a sampling-temperature change. Single runs per budget, one effort level, and self-audited transcripts limit strength; the RL rows use different environments and weaker PPO opponents than the original.
